title: RAG on Azure — Simply Explained
description:
Large language models do not know your company's data and their knowledge is frozen in time. This Simply Explained episode shows developers, architects and IT pros how retrieval-augmented generation on Azure solves that with Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Foundry, and how to start building it the right way.
In this episode
00:00 – What RAG is and why it matters01:36 – The two problems LLMs have03:05 – How retrieval-augmented generation works04:50 – Azure AI Search: indexing and searching06:37 – Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Foundry09:03 – Classic RAG vs. agentic RAG10:28 – End-to-end example12:10 – How to start building RAG on Azure
Key takeaways
RAG first retrieves relevant content from your own data and passes it to the model with the question, so answers are current and grounded instead of guessed from training memory.On Azure, Azure AI Search indexes and retrieves chunks with vector or hybrid search, Azure OpenAI generates the answer, and Azure AI Foundry wires the agent together.Start with your data, get retrieval right before adding the LLM, and choose agentic RAG only for complex questions where accuracy is worth the extra tokens and latency.
Worth quoting
“Ragh isn't a new model. It's not a bigger or better GPT. It's a different approach entirely.” – Mirko Peters (00:42)
“The LLM never sees your raw data. It only sees what the retrieval system hands it. It's not a drawback, so it's a security feature. Your sensitive documents stay in your own storage.” – Mirko Peters (04:08)
